name: Dhammadinna
role: Nun disciple, foremost in teaching the Dhamma
summary: Dhammadinna was a nun in the Buddha's lifetime, famous for answering her former husband's deep questions in the Cūḷavedalla Sutta. The Buddha called her foremost among nuns who teach.
about: According to Pali texts and commentary, Dhammadinna was the wife of Visakha of Rajagaha. After Visakha heard the Buddha teach and became a non-returner, he let her go forth as a nun. She lived in solitude and soon reached arahantship, with the four analytical knowledges. When she returned to Rajagaha, Visakha asked her about the Dhamma, and she answered so well that the Buddha praised her. This exchange is the Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44). The Anguttara Nikaya names her foremost among nuns who teach the Dhamma.
kidSummary: Dhammadinna was a Buddhist nun who lived in ancient India. Her husband asked a great many hard questions, and she answered each calmly and clearly. The Buddha said her answers were just what he would have said, and called her the best teacher among the nuns.

story.title: Leaving home
story.text: One day Visakha did not take Dhammadinna's outstretched hand. After he heard the Buddha teach, he let her become a nun and sent her in a golden palanquin.

story.title: Quiet practice
story.text: Dhammadinna lived alone and practised meditation. Soon she became an arahant and could explain the Dhamma with ease.

story.title: A visit from Visakha
story.text: Later she returned to Rajagaha. Visakha, now a lay follower, came and asked her many questions about the self, the path and feelings.

story.title: Clear answers
story.text: She answered one by one and, when his questions went beyond what she should answer, kindly told him to ask the Buddha.

story.title: The Buddha agrees
story.text: Visakha told the Buddha. The Buddha praised her and said her answers were right, and Visakha left happy.

teaches: Know when to send a questioner to the teacher
emblems: Role: foremost among nuns who teach the Dhamma

facts.text: The Pali dictionary says she answered her husband's deep questions as easily as someone cuts a lotus stalk with a knife.
Her one stanza in the Therigatha (1.12) says that a person whose mind is not bound to sense pleasures is heading upstream.
One day Visakha climbed the stairs without taking her outstretched hand and ate in silence; when she asked what was wrong, he told her.
She told her husband she could not live with her head held high by taking back what he had cast aside, so she asked to go forth.
Visakha wondered whether she came back so soon because she was unhappy, but thought it rude to ask, so he asked her about the teaching instead and kept going deeper.
After hearing the report, the Buddha called her his daughter, said she had no craving for past, future or present, and spoke a Dhammapada verse on having nothing to cling to.
In MN 44 she sorts the eightfold path into three groups: speech, action and livelihood as virtue; effort, mindfulness and concentration as concentration; view and resolve as discernment.
She tells Visakha there are pleasant, painful and neutral feelings, and that passion lurks in the pleasant, resistance in the painful and ignorance in the neutral.
Visakha keeps asking what lies beyond each answer, through clear knowing, release and unbinding, until she tells him he has gone too far and must stop pressing the limit.
She explains that pleasant feeling is pleasant while it lasts and painful when it changes, while painful feeling is the reverse.
She says in-and-out breaths count as bodily fabrications, directed thought as verbal ones, and perceptions and feelings as mental ones, because breath is tied to the body.
When a monk enters the cessation of perception and feeling, she says, speech stops first, then the body, then the mind; coming out reverses the order, with the mind first.
Visakha sent her to the nunnery in a golden palanquin, and one commentary says it was King Bimbisara who provided that palanquin.

quiz.q: Who asked Dhammadinna the questions in MN 44?
quiz.why: Visakha, her former husband, questioned her.

quiz.q: What did Dhammadinna do when his questions went beyond her limit?
quiz.why: She told him to ask the Buddha.

quiz.q: How was she carried to the nunnery?
quiz.why: Visakha sent her in a golden palanquin.

quiz.q: What did the Buddha call her among nuns?
quiz.why: She was named foremost among nuns who teach the Dhamma.
